title: Drawback Chess, But I Don't Know My Own Drawback
summary: Online Drawback Chess (drawback chess site, purple UI) vs random humans (e.g. 'happy yellow tiger') where the narrator does not know his own drawback (it is hidden) and must deduce it from which squares/moves are blocked (red squares). Game 1 (Black): his drawback was half the board's squares (32, randomised every turn) are forbidden to move to; opponent's was 'Savior complex' (when in check you must move your queen or lose). Game 2: his drawback was 'Eat your vegetables' (can't capture non-pawns until the opponent has only 4 pawns left). Goal: win one game. King-capture rules.
rules: Standard start; king-capture Drawback Chess rules (no check; capturing the king wins).
Each side gets a random drawback; in this episode the player's own drawback is hidden from him and from the viewer until the end.

Drawbacks seen: 'Can't move to half the board' (32 random squares highlighted red each turn are forbidden destinations); 'Savior complex' (when in check, you must move your queen or lose); 'Eat your vegetables' (you can't capture non-pawns until your opponent has only 4 pawns remaining); intro examples 'Noble seed'(only move knights?) and 'Can't move backwards'.
Forbidden squares/moves are shown red or simply unplayable in the UI.
End-of-game info board reveals both drawbacks.
win_condition: Capture the opponent's king; goal win one game.

Opponent should be a human-like mid-level bot, not Stockfish.
